sections.content: How many people are "chartered architectural technologists, planning officers and consultants"?

26,910 people

were counted on the census as "chartered architectural technologists, planning officers and consultants" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Chartered architectural technologists, planning officers and consultants direct or undertake planning for the development of urban and rural areas, provide architectural design services, and negotiate and manage the development from conception to completion of construction projects and lead on a variety of technical functions and solutions in the design of buildings and the layout of urban and rural areas.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 35 to 39 years. Of the whole working population 11.5% were aged 35 to 39 years. For people working as "chartered architectural technologists, planning officers and consultants", 15.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "chartered architectural technologists, planning officers and consultants" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "chartered architectural technologists, planning officers and consultants" included:

  • newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors
  • management consultants and business analysts
  • leisure and sports managers and proprietors

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "chartered architectural technologists, planning officers and consultants" there were more men than women (64.3% compared with 35.7%).

This means "chartered architectural technologists, planning officers and consultants" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business, media and public service professionals".

Men made up 64.3% and women made up 35.7% of "chartered architectural technologists, planning officers and consultants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "chartered architectural technologists, planning officers and consultants" included:

  • IT quality and testing professionals
  • prison service officers (below principal officer)
  • web design professionals

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "chartered architectural technologists, planning officers and consultants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "chartered architectural technologists, planning officers and consultants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "chartered architectural technologists, planning officers and consultants", 7.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (82% compared with 18%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (78.2%) than self-employed (21.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Bristol, City of, this is in the region of the South West.
